name: Flashlight (torch)
plain: Turns the camera LED on as a flashlight.
meaning: No personal data is read. Neither platform asks for permission, so any app can switch the light on while in the foreground.

android.permission: None (CAMERA is not needed for setTorchMode)
android.persistence: Torch turns off when the app leaves the foreground or another app takes the camera

ios.prompt_ui: None; torch control does not trigger the camera prompt
ios.note: Needs lockForConfiguration; the torch turns off when the capture session ends or the app backgrounds.

limits.headline: Can turn the flashlight on while the app is open, with no permission
can: Switch the camera light on and off
Set the brightness level (Android 13 and later, iPhone)
cannot: See any of your personal data
Keep the light on after the app goes to the background on iPhone
Take photos or video, which needs the camera prompt

story.what_it_is: Turns the camera light on so the phone works as a flashlight.
story.for_you: You swipe the control centre or tap a button and the light comes on. There is no pop up, since the light reads nothing about you. The light can also come on when an app scans a code in the dark.
story.for_makers: Apps use the light to help the camera work in low light, for scanners and for signals. It is also a classic pitch for tiny utility apps. It needs no permission, so it has been used as a cover for apps that ask for much more.

use_cases.example: A flashlight app turns on the LED with one tap.
A barcode scanner flips on the torch in a dark shop so a code can be read.
A video app lights a face while you record in a dark room.
A concert app turns the phone into a light show that blinks with the music.
A safety app flashes the torch to signal for help.
A deaf user gets a flash alert when the phone rings.
A treasure hunt game asks you to shine the light on a clue.

story.android_note: Android 13 adds brightness levels for the torch.
story.ios_note: The torch turns off when the app moves to the background or the camera stops.

technical_bounds: Camera light indicator rules do not cover the torch
